question: A 62-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 5-day history of swelling in his left arm. Two months ago, he was diagnosed with a deep venous thrombosis in the left calf. He has had a 7-kg (15-lb) weight loss in the last 3 months. He has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the past 25 years. His only medication is warfarin. Physical examination shows warm edema of the left forearm with overlying erythema and a tender, palpable cord-like structure along the medial arm. His lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Duplex sonography shows thrombosis of the left basilic and external jugular veins. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to confirm the underlying diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Deep venous thrombosis in left calf" -> "Swelling in left arm" -> "Tender, palpable cord-like structure along medial arm" -> "Warm edema of left forearm with erythema" -> "Thrombosis of left basilic and external jugular veins" -> "Possible diagnosis of superficial thrombophlebitis" -> 70%

CHAIN: "Weight loss" -> "Possible underlying malignancy" -> "Increased risk of hypercoagulability" -> "Deep venous thrombosis" -> "Swelling in left arm" -> "Thrombosis of left basilic and external jugular veins" -> "Possible diagnosis of superficial thrombophlebitis" -> 60%

CHAIN: "Smoking history" -> "Increased risk of thrombosis" -> "Deep venous thrombosis in left calf" -> "Swelling in left arm" -> "Thrombosis of left basilic and external jugular veins" -> "Possible diagnosis of superficial thrombophlebitis" -> 75%
analysis: Given the patient's history of deep venous thrombosis, current presentation of swelling in the left arm, and findings on physical examination and duplex sonography, the most appropriate next step to confirm the underlying diagnosis would be to check the serum D-dimer level. D-dimer is a fibrin degradation product that is elevated in conditions associated with thrombosis, and a positive result in this case would support the diagnosis of a new thrombus in the left arm.
